title: AWS CWI Exam Prep in Toledo, OH: 6-Day Course
description: Six-day AWS CWI exam prep for Toledo refinery, auto plant, solar and glass, shipyard and bridge welding: Part C code choice, Part B options and eligibility.
h1: AWS CWI Exam Preparation in Toledo: Six Days for Northwest Ohio Refinery, Automotive, Solar, Shipyard and Bridge Welding Inspectors
html:
Toledo is a place where refining, vehicle manufacturing and glass have overlapped for a century. Two refineries operate in the area, Jeeps and transmissions come off its assembly lines, the old Glass City now produces solar modules at scale, a port-owned shipyard repairs Great Lakes vessels, and turnpike and state highway crews keep rebuilding bridges across the Maumee. Every repair weld in a refinery unit, every bracket on a supplier's line and every girder on a bridge job needs someone qualified to accept it, and in northwest Ohio that person is often an AWS Certified Welding Inspector (CWI).

Atlantis NDT's six-day course prepares Toledo-area candidates for the CWI examination: pipefitters and welders moving toward inspection, refinery and contractor QC staff, plant maintenance leads, NDT technicians and engineers. AWS is the body that administers the examination and issues the certification, and each candidate applies to it directly and must personally meet its eligibility and vision rules. AWS does not endorse or approve the course, and Atlantis has no sight of examination content. There is no Atlantis classroom in Toledo. The six days can be studied online at your own pace with an instructor answering questions, delivered at an employer's site for a group, or taken one-to-one, online or in person at a location agreed at booking. The national AWS CWI exam prep page sets out what each of the six days covers.

Two refineries and a fourth-quarter turnaround

The US Energy Information Administration's refinery capacity report for January 2026 lists four operating refineries in Ohio with a combined 606,600 barrels per calendar day of crude distillation capacity. Two of them are in Toledo: Ohio Refining Company at 150,800 barrels per calendar day and Toledo Refining Company at 172,800. Cenovus Energy describes its refinery in Oregon, Ohio, just outside Toledo, as operating since 1919 with more than 600 employees and more than 500 contractors, and it has announced a five-year investment program across its two Ohio refineries. PBF Energy planned a 50- to 60-day turnaround at its Toledo refinery for the final quarter of 2026, including work on the fluid catalytic cracking unit, according to OPIS. Elsewhere in the region, the same EIA report lists Lima Refining Company at 183,000 barrels per calendar day, so three of the four Ohio refineries on the EIA list are in Toledo and Lima.

Refinery welding is pressure work. Piping is built and repaired to ASME B31.3, procedures and welders are qualified to ASME Section IX, and repairs to pressure vessels follow the owner's inspection program under documents such as API 510. A CWI on a refinery contract typically checks fit-up, preheat and interpass temperature, reviews welder qualifications against the procedure, carries out visual acceptance and coordinates the NDT and pressure testing the code requires. For that career the ASME option for Part C, Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3, is the natural choice. Background: ASME Section IX and ASME B31.3.

Jeeps, transmissions and the supplier base

Stellantis employs more than 4,300 people at the Toledo Assembly Complex, which builds the Jeep Wrangler and Gladiator, and in October 2025 the company said a new midsize truck would be built there as part of its US investment plan, adding about 900 jobs according to Ohio's governor. GM's Toledo Propulsion Systems plant employs around 1,650 people and in 2026 received new investment to raise capacity for the 10-speed transmissions used in GM's light-duty trucks.

Vehicle body joining is dominated by robots and resistance welding, so a CWI in this cluster is more often found at suppliers of frames, brackets, exhaust and chassis parts, at tooling and fixture builders, and in the maintenance departments that repair plant equipment and structures. In those roles the CWI syllabus pays off on arc-welded parts, where size, profile and discontinuities are checked against the drawing and the customer's weld standard.

From Glass City to solar modules

Toledo's glass history still shapes its industry. Owens Corning is based in Toledo, and Libbey has its headquarters in the city. First Solar, which started in the Toledo area in 1999, runs three factories and a research and development center at its Northwest Ohio campus, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland, and in 2025 Pilkington North America converted a float glass line at its Rossford factory to make transparent conductive oxide glass for First Solar. The same Cleveland Fed article noted that nearly 16 percent of Toledo-area residents worked in manufacturing in 2023, one of the highest shares in the bank's district, and quoted First Solar's chief supply chain officer saying that finding skilled workers is an ongoing challenge.

Glass and module plants weld less than a fabrication shop does, but they are large continuous-process sites with furnaces, conveyors, structural platforms, utility and process piping, and a steady stream of capital projects. The maintenance and construction contractors who build and repair that equipment need welders and inspectors who can work to AWS D1.1 for steel structures and to the owner's specification, often ASME B31.3 or B31.1, for piping.

A port-owned shipyard

The Toledo Shipyard is owned by the Toledo-Lucas County Port Authority and has been operated by IRONHEAD Marine since 2006. The yard handles dry-dock ship repair, hull work, mechanical repairs and rebuilds, and blasting and painting, and its heavy industrial fabrication includes welding that the Port Authority describes as certified under AWS and ABS standards, alongside plate rolling and plasma and oxy-fuel cutting, in a 20,000-square-foot high bay with two 20-ton cranes.

Ship repair to classification society rules is not one of the Part C options, so a shipyard candidate normally takes AWS D1.1 for the structural and fabrication side of the yard's work and learns the class rules separately, alongside the surveyors who apply them.

Turnpike decks and state bridges

The Ohio Turnpike's 2026 construction program, published in April, included redecking the westbound mainline bridge over the Maumee River at milepost 63, between Lucas and Wood counties, with completion estimated for November 15, 2026 and the eastbound structure to follow in 2027 and 2028. In Fulton County the mainline bridge over Bad Creek is being widened and redecked through 2027. Steel members on public bridges are normally fabricated and repaired to AWS D1.5, the Bridge Welding Code, with the owner's specifications on top.

A Toledo inspector who wants to work for steel fabricators supplying ODOT or turnpike projects, or for the consultants who inspect that work, should consider D1.5 for Part C. Reading: AWS D1.5.

A Part C table for northwest Ohio

Your workCode bookWhy it fits
Refinery and chemical plant piping, vessel repair crewsASME Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3The qualification and process piping documents refinery contracts cite most
Structural steel, shipyard fabrication, plant platformsAWS D1.1:2020The general structural welding code for steel
Bridge steel for ODOT and turnpike workAWS D1.5:2020, with Clause 12Bridge fabrication, including fracture-critical members
Pipeline and gas distribution contractorsAPI 1104, 22nd editionPipeline girth welds and their acceptance
Aluminum fabricationAWS D1.2:2014The structural aluminum code on the AWS list

AWS lists the edition for each option, and it can be older than the one on your shelf, so study the edition AWS names. More reading: AWS D1.1 and WPS, PQR and WPQ explained.

Owens Community College and the Northwest Ohio Section

Owens Community College offers an associate of applied science in welding that trains students in stick, gas, MIG and TIG welding, and students who excel may take the college's plate or pipe welding pre-certification test. Its pipe welding certificate is a 10-credit, one-semester program at the Dana Center for Advanced Manufacturing, a 59,000-square-foot facility, ending with a pre-certification and testing course that follows ASME Section IX; the credits carry into the associate degree. That pipe focus suits the refinery and plant work around Toledo.

The AWS Northwest Ohio Section, in District 11, has a student chapter at Owens Community College. In 2026 it held its first annual Tech Night at Monroe Community College in March and its Donald J. Leonhardt golf outing in June. If you cannot find a current meeting notice, the sections page on aws.org lists every section by district.

Part B from northwest Ohio

Toledo is better placed for Part B than many cities. AWS's November 2026 list of CWI training locations includes Detroit and Cleveland, with Chicago and Indianapolis also on it. The Hobart Institute of Welding Technology in Troy, Ohio, lists more than a dozen 2026 CWI sessions with AWS exam site codes and says it conducts the Part B exam on the second Friday of each course; ask AWS whether a given session is open to you if you are not taking that course. Parts A and C are computer-based at Prometric test centers once AWS has accepted your application.

AWS closes US applications six weeks ahead of the Part B date, and it requires 72 percent on every part. Get the vision test and experience records in order first, then choose the session and leave room for a possible retake. The CWI exam cost calculator helps you plan the travel and the time.

Part B deserves more practice than many candidates give it. AWS hands you its own tools and specimens and asks 46 questions built around them, and many of the marks come from applying a procedure or qualification record you have just been given, not from shop instinct. Practise with fillet gauges, a bridge cam gauge, a hi-lo gauge and calipers until the readings are automatic, and get used to comparing a measured value against the acceptance criteria printed in the documents in front of you rather than the ones you use at work.

Two routes into the exam: pipe welder and plant technician

Consider two hypothetical Toledo candidates. The first is a pipe welder with a high school diploma who has spent six years on refinery maintenance and turnaround crews, fitting and welding carbon and chrome piping to qualified procedures. With a diploma AWS asks for five years of welding-related experience, and this record can show it, provided each contractor can confirm the dates and duties. The second has an associate degree in engineering technology and three years as a quality technician at a manufacturing plant, checking welded assemblies against drawings and keeping weld records; with that degree AWS asks for two years, so the open question is whether the work counts as welding-related, which AWS decides.

A third hypothetical case comes from the port: a welder who finished a vocational program, then spent four years at a ship repair and fabrication yard on hull plate, structural repairs and fitting. Completed trade or vocational courses bring the AWS requirement to four years, so the record is borderline in length, and every month of it needs a name that can confirm it. Waiting a few more months and applying with a margin is usually wiser than applying on the exact minimum.

Both should build their evidence the same way: employer, dates, processes and materials, the procedures or standards followed, and any inspection, documentation or qualification-test duties, each with a name to verify it. Both also need a passed vision test on AWS's visual acuity form, recent enough to be valid on exam day. More detail is in the CWI requirements guide.

Bringing the six days to a contractor or plant

A mechanical contractor, refinery maintenance group or manufacturer with several candidates can host the six days at its own site. The practical work can use the site's own coupons, weld samples and gauges, and the code work can follow the book most of the group will use, the ASME option for pipe crews or D1.1 for fabricators. Because the employer sets the weeks, the course can be placed clear of a turnaround or a model launch.

The certification still belongs to each person. Every candidate applies to AWS individually, provides their own vision record and experience evidence, and sits each exam part under their own name.

After the CWI: refinery inspection, NDT and more

Many Toledo CWIs stay in refinery and plant work, where the next credential is often an API individual certification: API 510 for pressure vessels or API 570 for piping. Atlantis offers self-paced API exam preparation; API administers those examinations and certifies inspectors. Others add NDT methods, which require training and certification by the employer under its written practice; Atlantis provides training based on ASNT SNT-TC-1A, including VT Level 2, UT Level 2 and MT Level 2, with the employer certifying afterwards. AWS renews the CWI at three-year intervals and requires recertification at the nine-year mark.

Local pages: NDT training in Toledo, refining NDT training in Toledo, ultrasonic testing in Toledo, magnetic particle testing in Toledo, and CWI exam prep in Detroit, Cleveland and Columbus.

Sending a Toledo enquiry

Tell us how many people need preparation, the format you want, the code each candidate plans to use for Part C and when you expect to sit the exam. For a group, give the site location and the weeks that avoid outages or launches. If you are not sure the experience will satisfy AWS, describe it briefly and we will point out what to check with AWS. We quote each format on request, and you will hear back from us within one business day.

faq.q: Is there an AWS section in Toledo?
faq.a: The AWS Northwest Ohio Section, part of District 11, serves the area and has a student chapter at Owens Community College. Its 2026 events included a Tech Night at Monroe Community College in March and a golf outing in June.

faq.q: Where can a Toledo candidate take Part B?
faq.a: At an AWS seminar location. The November 2026 AWS list included Detroit, Cleveland, Chicago and Indianapolis, and the Hobart Institute in Troy, Ohio, lists 2026 sessions with AWS site codes. Parts A and C are taken at Prometric centers.

faq.q: Which Part C code should a refinery welder choose?
faq.a: Usually the ASME option, Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3, because refinery piping and qualification work is written around those documents. Choose AWS D1.1 if your work is mostly structural.

faq.q: Does the CWI replace API 510 or API 570 for refinery inspection?
faq.a: No. The CWI covers welding inspection. API 510 and API 570 are separate API individual certifications for in-service inspection of vessels and piping, administered by API.

faq.q: Can a shipyard welder use classification society rules for Part C?
faq.a: No. Class rules are not on the AWS list of Part C code books. Shipyard candidates usually take AWS D1.1 for the structural and fabrication side of the work.

faq.q: I am an Owens Community College welding graduate. How much experience do I need?
faq.a: With an associate degree in welding, AWS lists two years of welding-related experience; with completed trade or vocational courses, four. AWS decides which applies to you and whether your work counts.

faq.q: Can our contractor schedule the six days around a turnaround?
faq.a: Yes. With the corporate format the employer chooses the weeks and the six days are delivered at its site. Each candidate still applies to AWS individually.

faq.q: Is the course endorsed by AWS?
faq.a: No. AWS has not approved or endorsed the course, and Atlantis has no access to examination content. AWS administers the examination and issues the certification.

faq.q: Is there an Atlantis classroom in Toledo?
faq.a: No. There is no Atlantis classroom in Toledo. The course is taken online, at an employer's site for a group, or one-to-one online or in person at a location agreed when booking. Atlantis offices are in Houston and Hyderabad.

faq.q: How do I get a quote from Toledo?
faq.a: Use the enquiry link on this page and tell us the format, the number of candidates and the Part C code. We quote on request and reply within one business day.
